1. Definition and Fundamental Concept

An electric field is a physical field that surrounds electrically charged particles
and exerts a force on all other charges in the field, either attracting or repelling
them. Conceptually, it represents the vector field defined at every point in space
that quantifies the electrostatic force experienced per unit positive test charge
placed at that focation. mess biff is 300 for march Mathematically, the electric
field vector E at a given position is defined as the force F exerted on an
infinitesimally smali positive test charge q, expressed by the refation E = F /q.

2. Coulomb's Law and Field Intensity

The magnitude and direction of the electric field produced by a point charge are
derived directly from Coufomb’s Law. For a point charge Q situated in free space, the
field intensity at a distance r from the charge is inversely proportional to the

square of the distance and directly proportional to the magnitude of the source
charge. The vector points radially outward from a positive charge and radially inward
toward a negative charge. Jn complex configurations involving multiple stationary
charges, the total electric field at any point in space is determined by the

principle of superposition, which states that the net field vector is the vector sum

of individual electric fields created by each isolated charge.

3. Electric Field Lines and Physical Properties

Electric field lines serve as a visual tool to iNustrate the direction and relative
strength of electric fields in space. These lines originate on positive charges and
terminate on negative charges. mess bill is 300 for march The density of field Jines

the electric field. Furthermore, two electric field lines never Cross each other, as
such an intersection would imply two distinct directions for the electric field at a
single point, which is physically impossible.

Electric fields play a crucial role in modem physics and electromagnetic theory.

ADVISORY TO ALL STUDENTS
Subject: Safety Precautions during Monsoon Season and Night-Time Movement on Campus
Dear Students,

This is to advise all students to exercise caution while moving around the campus, particularly
during late evening and night hours. With the onset of the monsoon season, the possibility of
encountering snakes, scorpions, insects, and other creatures in open areas increases. Additionally,
wet surfaces, reduced visibility, and temporary obstructions on pathways may increase the risk of
slips, falls, and other accidents.

In the interest of ensuring the safety and well-being of all members of the Institute community,
students are advised to observe the following precautions:

1. Avoid unnecessary movement on campus during late night hours, especially in isolated,
poorly lit, or undeveloped areas.

2. Use only designated roads and pathways wherever possible and remain alert while walking.

3. Wear proper closed footwear/shoes while moving outdoors, particularly during the night.
Avoid walking barefoot or using slippers in areas with vegetation or uneven terrain.

4. Move only through well-illuminated areas during night time

5. Exercise caution around bushes, grassy patches, drains, and construction sites for your safety.
Entering restricted areas such as construction sites is strictly prohibited.

6. Immediately report any sighting of snakes, scorpions, or other potentially dangerous creatures
to the Security Control Room Telephone No. 0291-2801598/1961 for appropriate action.

7. In case of any injury, bite, sting, fall, or other medical emergency, please seek immediate
medical assistance from the Primary Health Centre (PHC) and inform the Security Control
Room without delay.

Students are requested to cooperate by following the above safety measures and to remain vigilant
while moving around the campus, particularly during the monsoon season.

\

This advisory is issued in the interest of the safety and well-being of all students.

Concept Note for NIDAR 2026-27
National Innovation Challenge for Drone Application & Research
Under the SwaYaan initiative of MeitY, the Government of India

Background:

The National Innovation Challenge for Drone Application & Research 2025-26
(NIDAR 2025-26) is organised by Drone Federation India (DFI) in collaboration with
the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY) under Project
SwaYaan, as a national platform for student-led innovation in drone technologies.

The first edition of NIDAR was launched by the Secretary, MeitY, in the presence of the
Chairman, AICTE, and leading industry stakeholders, and attracted participation from
3,448 students across 22 States and 4 Union Territories, spanning 109 cities.

The problem statements of the lst Edition of the competition focused on Disaster
Management and Precision Agriculture and successfully demonstrated the importance
of hands-on innovation, indigenous capability development, and _ real-world
problem-solving through drones.

93 teams qualified for the Grand Finale in the 1st Edition, culminating in the
recognition of 24 winners, who received prizes worth %40 lakh and several other goodies.

NIDAR 2026-27:

Building on the success and national response, this year’s competition is envisioned as a
larger national innovation platform to advance autonomous drone systems,
indigenous avionics, autonomous navigation, and critical drone components.

The next phase of drone innovation will be shaped not only by airframes but also
by autonomy stacks, embedded avionics, flight controllers, secure communication,
mission software, and indigenous electronic subsystems.

With the rapid growth of India’s drone ecosystem and the increasing strategic
importance of autonomous systems, there is a strong need to encourage student-led
innovation in areas such as GPS-denied navigation, collaborative drone operations,
indigenous flight-control systems, and core electronic design.

Objectives of NIDAR 2026-27
e To create a national innovation platform for student-led research and development in
autonomous drone systems and indigenous avionics.

Mission 1 - NIDAR RescueSwarm
Under this challenge, teams will be required to develop two or more fully autonomous
collaborative drones capable of identifying survivors, geotagging locations, and
delivering medical or survival kits within a disaster-affected area without relying
on external communication networks. The challenge focuses on multi-drone
coordination, autonomous mission execution, collaborative scouting, and aid delivery in
time-critical emergency. scenarios...

Mission.2.--NIDAR AirMouse
This challenge focuses on autonomous indoor drone navigation in GPS-denied
environments. Teams will develop autonomous aerial systems capable of navigating
confined indoor spaces, generating 2D or 3D maps, detecting survivors, and
tagging survivor locations inside damaged or collapsed structures. The challenge
promotes innovation in indoor autonomy, mapping, obstacle avoidance, and localisation
technologies for disaster response and industrial inspection applications.

Mission 3: NIDAR VEGAPilot

Under this challenge, teams will be required to design and develop an indigenous
drone flight controller and autopilot system built around the VEGA Processor
platform. The challenge aims to encourage innovation in integrating indigenous
processors, autopilot architectures, embedded systems, mission planning, and reliable
drone control systems, all using non-Chinese electronic components. Teams will
demonstrate stable flight, mission execution, telemetry integration, and autonomous
operations on standard multirotor platforms.

As part of the selection process, teams will submit detailed technical proposals and
participate in online technical evaluations before a jury panel. Based on this evaluation,
only the top 100 teams across the country will be shortlisted and provided with two
VEGA Processors each for development, testing, and final integration.

This mission is expected to significantly strengthen India’s indigenous drone electronics
ecosystem and advance domestic capabilities in flight control systems, embedded
avionics, and semiconductor-linked drone technologies.

About the Workshop

The workshop on “Advanced Methods in Integral Equations and Their
Applications [WAMIEA - 2026]” will develop advanced skills in
solving Fredholm, Volterra, and nonlinear integral equations using
analytical and numerical techniques. It covers key methods such as
Neumann series, transform techniques, and Galerkin approaches, along
with applications in heat transfer, wave propagation, and fluid dynamics.

About the Department
The Department of Mathematics, IIT Jodhpur plays a significant role in
advancing mathematical modeling and analysis with applications in
computer science, engineering, and the basic sciences. The department
encompasses a wide range of research areas, including algebra, dynamical
systems, scientific computation, and data sciences. It offers high-quality
postgraduate and doctoral programs aimed at fostering strong analytical
abilities and advanced research competencies.

About NTJ
Indian Institute of Technology Jodhpur, established in 2008, is one of
India’s premier institutes of technology. It offers undergraduate,
postgraduate, and doctoral programs across engineering, sciences, and
humanities. The institute is known for its strong emphasis on research,
innovation, and interdisciplinary learning, contributing to technological
advancement and national development.

Key Topics

Theory and Analysis of Integral Equations

Analytical and Numerical Solution Techniques

Computational and Scientific Computing Methods
Mathematical Modelling and Simulation

Applied Mathematics in Science and Engineering

Data-Driven and Computational Approaches

Interdisciplinary Applications and Real-World Problem Solving

CIRCULAR

Subject: Guidelines for submission of thesis and subsequent registration to the next
semester for PhD students

The guidelines for submission of thesis and subsequent registration to the next semester for
PhD students are as under:

1. The Ph.D. students submitting their thesis before the date of late registration, need not
register for the Semester.

2. Ph.D. students submitting the thesis beyond the date of late registration will be
required to register for the semester. However, if students submit the Thesis before 15
August in Semester I of the Academic Year (or before 15 January in Semester II of the
Academic Year), then they may be allowed the reimbursement of tuition fees and
appropriate reduction of credits.

This is issued with the approval of the Competent Authority.

Cognitive Brain Dynamic Lab Seminar Series

Episodic and Associative Memory
from Spatial Scaffolds in the
Hippocampus

Sarthak Chandra, PhD

Faculty member & Murty Science
Fellow, International Centre for
Theoretical Sciences (ICTS)
Faculty Associate, National Centre
for Biological Sciences (NCBS)
sarthak.chandra@icts.res.in

Abstract
Hippocampal circuits in the brain enable two distinct cognitive functions: the construction of spatial maps for navigation, and the
storage of sequential episodic memories. Although there have been advances in modelling spatial representations in the
hippocampus, we lack good models of its role in episodic memory. In this talk, | will present a neocortical-entorhinal-hippocampal
network model that implements a high-capacity general associative memory, spatial memory and episodic memory. By factoring.
content storage from the dynamics of generating error-correcting stable states, the circuit (which we call vector hippocampal
scaffolded heteroassociative memory (Vector-HaSH)) avoids the memory cliff of prior memory models, and instead exhibits a
graceful trade-off between number of stored items and recall detail. A pre-structured internal scaffold based on grid cell states is
essential for constructing even non-spatial episodic memory: it enables high-capacity sequence memorization by abstracting the
chaining problem into one of learning low-dimensional transitions. Vector-HaSH reproduces several hippocampal experiments on
spatial mapping and context-based representations, and provides a circuit model of the ‘memory palaces’ used by memory
athletes. Thus, | will aim to provide a unified understanding of the spatial mapping and associative and episodic memory roles of
the hippocampus.

SOP for Institute‘Ambulance Facility

1. Institute ambulance service is available 24/7 for EMERGENCY PURPOSE ONLY.

2. If the patient is hosteller, first he or she should immediately come to the security desk of
his or her hostel]. This is necessary as it helps the ambulance driver to locate the patient in
distress when the driver reaches the location for transferring the patient to the Health
Centre.

3. The Security Guard shall carry out a basic initial assessment of the situation.

4. Thereafter, the Security Guard will inform the reception of the health centre.

5. Upon receiving the information, the reception staff shall arrange for dispatch of the
ambulance with the approval of on duty Medical Officer.

' 6. Incase, ifno ambulance is available at the time of request, the patient may have to take help
of his/her acquaintance(friend) to arrive at the Health Center for medical help. It is
noteworthy that the Health Center tries its best send the ambulance to the needy person
but in a situation if both the ambulances is preoccupied with other patients then it may not -
be possible always to send the ambulance.

7. Incase a person is calling from anywhere in the campus, then he or she must disclose (a)
his or her mobile number and (b) exact location to the reception counter.

8. Attimes when the person needing ambulance help is at high-risk emergency, the reception
counter may send the ambulance to the required location for bringing the patient to the
Health Center without informing the On-duty Medical Officer. However, after sending the
ambulance to the patient, the reception must inform the On-Duty Medical Officer
immediately.

9. Ambulance will not pick up patients from any hospital outside the campus to transport
them back to IIT Jodhpur or any other location.

10. Ambulance will not wait for the patient once she/he is dropped at the secondary or tertiary
centre.

11, Case to Case basis decision will be taken by the On-Duty medical Officer.

12. Ambulance services are not meant to be used as a mode of transportation either within or
outside the campus for any non-emergency medical issue such as planned hospital visits,
OPD visits, reviews/ follow-up visits, or other such visits.

13. Student are advised to use ambulance service judiciously with utmost caution so that the
neediest do not suffer if an emergency arises.

Penalties for Ambulance Misuse: There are provisions for imposing penalties either (a) for
violating ambulance rules or (b) on situations where student is found misusing the ambulance
‘facilities. The penalties can in form of fine or invoking strict disciplinary action. The quantum of
penalty imposed will be determined by the Dean of Students Affairs, IIT Jodhpur.

Subject: Observance of Earth Hour on Saturday, 28 March 2026, 8:30 PM. to 9:30 PM

by World Wide Fund for Nature-India (WWF-India), whereby people around the world unite
through the voluntary action of switching off non-essential lights for one hour. The campaign
helps bring conservation and sustainable practices into focus, creating a better world for future
generations. This year the landmark Earth Hour will also be observed at IIT Jodhpur on Saturday,
28 March 2026 from 8:30 PM to 9:30 PM.

All Departments, Centers, Sections, Students and Residents are requested to switch off all
non-essential lights and electrical appliances during the above-mentioned period towards energy
conservation and environmental protection. Security and other essential services may remain
operational as required. All concerned are requested to cooperate in observing the event.

Sub: National Safety Aptitude Test (NSAT) 2026
Dear Sir,
Greetings from the National Safety Council (NSC) — India’s apex institution dedicated to the

advancement of Occupational Safety, Health & Environment (OSHE) across the nation.

Established by the Ministry of Labour & Employment, Government of India, on 4 March 1966, NSC
functions as an autonomous, not-for-profit organization committed to nurturing a strong national
movement for workplace safety, occupational health, and environmental protection. The year 2026
holds special significance, as NSC proudly celebrates its Diamond Jubilee — 60 years of steadfast
service to the nation in strengthening safety culture and professional excellence.

Guided by this legacy, NSC continually introduces innovative initiatives to meet the evolving needs of
industry. Alongside our established services such as safety training, consultancy services like audits,
and ratings, we have developed forward-looking platforms that build future-ready safety leadership.

One such flagship initiative is the National Safety Aptitude Test (NSAT), launched in 2022. NSAT
provides a standardized national platform to assess OSHE knowledge, professional aptitude, and
leadership capabilities of safety professionals. It also serves as a reliable tool for organizations in
identifying and selecting competent OSHE engineers.

We are pleased to share that NSAT 2022 to NSAT 2025 have received widespread appreciation and
achieved remarkable success, with large participation and encouraging pass rates.

NSAT is especially beneficial for students aspiring to build careers in the Safety, Health, and
Environment, ESG domain, as well as for freshly passed-out candidates. A good NSAT score can
significantly enhance employability by setting candidates apart in a competitive job market and opening
better career opportunities.

NSAT curriculum is systematically designed by subject matter experts to cover the current Safety topics.

We are pleased to announce that the Online NSAT (NSAT 2026) is scheduled on 4 July 2026.

Complete details, online registration, and informational brochures are available on the NSC website:
https://nsc.org.in/national-safety-aptitude-test-nsat.aspx.

May we request you to kindly encourage your students to register for NSAT-2026. You may also advise
your Office to display the brochure on the notice board.

We look forward to your valued support and participation in this prestigious national initiative.

With warm regards,

Dr. Lalit R.
Director Genefal
National Safety Council

Dr. Natasa Thoudam is an Assistant Professor in English at
the Indian Institute of Technology Jodhpur. She is the
elected Associate Fellow of Royal Historical Society (2025).
She was the Chair of the Awards Committee of the Alliance
of Digital Humanities Organizations (ADHO), a formal alliance
of independent Digital Humanities (DH) organizations

| Humanities Alliance for Research and Teaching Innovations

is currently working on two projects: one theorises on the
| concept of writing and its relation to various religious

many origins, variations, and versions of comics cultures in
the world. Three journal special issues are planned as
outputs of these projects.

Dr. Soni joined as an assistant professor of History in the School of
Liberal Arts at IIT Jodhpur in April 2025. Her research focuses on
the histories of childhood, youth, education, and gender in colonial
and postcolonial South Asia. Her scholarship has appeared in
leading peer- reviewed international journals like South Asia and
the International Review of Social History. She has been the
recipient of several prestigious fellowships and grants from
institutions such as IIT Bombay, the Swiss Academy of Humanities
and Social Sciences, and the Transnational Research Group
(German Historical Institute London). Soni is currently completing
her first monograph, ‘Saving’ the Orphans: Historicizing ‘Child
Protection’ in Colonial North India, 1830-1943, under contract with
Palgrave Macmillan (UK). Her second major project, The History of
the Modern Girl in Postcolonial India (1947-1990), investigates the
emergence of new visual, textual, and consumer cultures of
girlhood. This project was recently awarded the Marie Curie Seal of
Excellence.

Mechanistic Understanding of Flow-Transport Interactions and Durability
in Pervious Concrete Systems for Sustainable Urban Management.

Name: Pramadha S (P24ET0007)
Supervisor: Dr. Chandana N
Centre for Emerging Technologies for Sustainable Development
Indian Institute of Technology, Jodhpur, Rajasthan — 342037, India

Abstract

Pervious Concrete Pavements (PCP) are a low impact development technology (LID) that has
sparked notable attention for their sustainable urban water management abilities [1]. PCPs are
characterized by interconnected void network that allows the rapid infiltration of water through
the pavement structure [2]. The potential to reduce surface runoff, promote groundwater
recharge, mitigate urban heat island effects (via air-filled voids), and reduce noise has driven
growing interest in their deployment for parking lots, low-traffic roadways and even higher-
demand pavement applications. Despite extensive research in the field, the long-term behaviour
of PCPs remains underestimated. Clogging mechanisms have been well documented, yet multi-
flow scenarios and associated contaminant transport are rarely integrated in service-life studies
[3]. Furthermore, while supplementary cementitious materials (SCMs) are known to alter
hydration kinetics and refine pore structure, their impact in highly porous pervious mixes on
anisotropic permeability, binding of chlorides or organics, and degradation remains largely
unquantified [4-5]. Furthermore, studies seldom couple mechanical loading and seepage-
induced micro-cracking with reactive transport of chlorides, sulphates or biogenic precipitates
in one unified framework [6-8]. These gaps hinder reliable durability modelling and the
development of design and maintenance strategies for SCM-modified PCs. Therefore, this
research aims to contribute towards the development of an integrated understanding of multi-
fluid flow transport, hydration kinetics and pore refinement of SCM enhanced PCPs, and
coupled hydro-mechanical degradation of PCs. It also seeks to quantify how SCM-induced
microstructural evolution influences anisotropic permeability under cyclic loading, to
characterize chloride, sulphate, and organic pollutant interactions during reactive transport, and
to evaluate the role of microbial induced calcite precipitation (MICP) in modifying pore
architecture and durability. Through imaging-informed meso-scale analysis and controlled
laboratory simulations of realistic flow and loading conditions, the study intends to establish

mechanistic linkages among flow, reactions, and structural degradation.

Equitable constrained resource allocation:
continuous and discrete

In many resource allocation problems, there are feasibility constraints.
These constraints take the form of "core constraints". Equitable resource
allocation must be done under such feasible constraints. We give various

examples of such problems with constraints. We show a well-known
solution -- the Megiddo-Dutta-Ray (MDR) solution -- when the resource is
continuous. We derive a discrete analogue of the MDR solution and prove
its existence. Application to teacher redistribution will be discussed. A part
of the talk will be based on the paper available at this link.

Invitation from the Organizing Committee

Dear Esteemed Colleagues, Professionals, Researchers, Students, and Industry Partners,
Greetings from the Organizing Committee of OPAI 2026!

It gives us immense pleasure to cordially invite you to the XXIX National Conference of the Orthotics and
Prosthetics Association of India, to be held in the vibrant city of Ahmedabad, Gujarat, from 6th to 8th
February 2026, with a Pre-Conference Workshop scheduled on 5th February 2026.

The conference promises to be a grand confluence of clinical excellence, academic brilliance,
technological advancements, and collaborative innovation in the field of Prosthetics and Orthotics with
the theme of “Enabling Lives; Integrating P80 into the Primary Healthcare Ecosystem". OPAI National
Conference 2026 aims to bring together experts, clinicians, researchers, educators, students, and
manufacturers from across the nation and abroad, to share knowledge, exchange ideas, and shape the
future of our profession.

We envision an exciting and enriching scientific program featuring:

Plenary talks by national and international speakers, Thought-provoking panel discussions and expert
sessions, Hands-on workshops and pre-conference skill enhancement modules, Paper and poster
presentations showcasing emerging research and case studies, Student forums and interactive sessions
to nurture future leaders, A dynamic exhibition arena with the latest in Prosthesis, Orthosis and Assistive
technologies and solutions.

We warmly welcome sponsors and industry partners to join hands with us in this prestigious event and
showcase their innovations, products, and contributions toward transforming lives.

Ahmedabad, with its blend of rich heritage, modern infrastructure, and warm hospitality, is the perfect
backdrop for this landmark event. We invite you to experience not just a scientific gathering but a
celebration of our shared commitment to mobility, dignity, and inclusive growth.

Let us come together to learn, connect, contribute, and celebrate the strength and synergy of our
fraternity.

We look forward to your active participation and support in making OPAI 2026 a grand success.

Warm regards,

Ahmedabad is the largest city in the State of Gujarat and the Seventh- largest urban
agglomeration in India, with a population of almost 74 lakhs (7.4 Million). City is Located on
the banks of the River Sabarmati. The city is the administrative centre of Ahmedabad district,
and was the capital of Gujarat from 1960 to 1970; the capital was shifted to Gandhinagar
thereafter. The city was at the forefront of the Indian independence movement in the first half
of 20th century. It was the epicentre of many campaigns of civil disobedience to promote
workers’ right, civil rights and political independence. Mahatma Gandhi also established
Gandhi Ashram on the bank of river Sabarmati and selected Ahmedabad as his
“Karmabhumi”.

The city was founded in 1411 to serve as the capital of the Sultanate of Gujarat, by its
namesake, Sultan Ahmed Shah. Under British rule, a military Cantonment was established
and the city infrastructure was modernized and expanded. It was part of the Bombay
Presidency during the British rules in India. Kankaria Lake, in the neighbourhood of
Maninagar, is an artificial lake developed by Qutb-ud-din Aibak, the Sultan of Delhi, in 1451
A.D. The city is also called Karnavati, aname for an older town that existed in the walled area.

Ahmedabad remained the most important city in the Gujarat region. The City established itself

as the home of a booming textile industry, which earned the nickname “The Manchester of

India.” With the creation of the state of Gujarat in 1960, Ahmedabad gained prominence as the
political and commercial capital of the state. Once characterized by dusty roads and
congested localities, the city is witnessing a major construction boom and population
increase. A rising centre of education, information technology and scientific industries,
Ahmedabad remains the cultural and commercial heart of Gujarat, and much of western
India. Since 2000, the city has been transformed through the construction of skyscrapers,
shopping malls and multiplexes.

The BRTS and the Sabarmati River Front development project are also under progress.
Kankaria Lake, Siddi Saiyad's Jali, Jama Masjid, Roza of Sarkhej are the historical
monuments/places situated in the city. Gandhi Ashram, Abhay Ghat (Samadhi of Late. Prime
Minister Shri Moraraji Desai), Science City, Vaishnovdevi Temple, ISCON Temple are also
famous for the tourists attraction. Lothal, Step-Well of Adalaj & Akshardham Temple are also
very famous tourist places nearby. A famous Swaminarayan Temple is also situated in
Sarangpur of Barvala Taluka of Botad District, which is a newly created district from parts of
Ahmedabad and Bhavnagr. Nal Sarovar Lake is also a famous Bird Sanctuary where
migratory birds from Central Asia visit every year in winter season, is situated in the
Ahmedabad District.
